I think that the only long-term solution to the problem of over-upvoted low content memes, is to use a decrementing vote counter in the top right, where your number of votes available decreases as you spend them. This way voaters feel that there is a need to exercise more caution when spending votes, and not to spend them unwisely on low content posts.

Suppose we have 2 users and 3 posts:

Post A is an extremely dank meme.

Post B is an informative article about topic X.

Post C is an informative article about topic Y.

User 1 really likes X and upvotes Post B. User 2 really likes Y and upvotes Post C. User 1 and 2 also kind of like Post A, the dank meme, so they upvote that as well.

What is the result?

The result is that the dank meme is pushed to the top of the page, despite the fact that no user on the site actually liked the dank meme the most, and that they all had a different post they cared about more.

How can we prevent this ranking failure?

We can apply a scarcity to votes by capping the maximum votes one can sit on to a multiple of one's comment score, put an explicit decrementing available vote counter in the top right of the interface, and contiually regenerate users supply of available votes at a rate of 5% of their maximum votes per hour.
